O.outcome_detail: predicting chronic absence, low GPA, and course failure

cells.quote: The study finds that the prior performance early warning system and the algorithm using the same-percentage risk score cutoffs are similarly accurate. Both approaches successfully identify most of the students who ultimately are chronically absent, have a low grade point average, or fail a course.
cells.note: The text reports similar accuracy but does not report an equivalence test or adequate power.

O.outcome_detail: predicting suspensions

cells.quote: In contrast, the algorithm with 10-percent cutoffs is good at targeting the students who are most likely to experience an academic problem; this approach has the advantage in predicting suspensions, which are rarer and harder to predict than the other outcomes.
cells.note: The study text describes an advantage but does not provide a printed effect size.

O.outcome_detail: accuracy of prior-performance flags and algorithm predictions

cells.quote: Both the prior performance flags and the algorithm are less accurate when predicting outcomes for students who are Black.
cells.note: The study reports lower accuracy for Black students but does not specify the comparison group or provide a printed effect size.

O.outcome_detail: access to and participation in WIL

cells.quote: Employing technology to support and deliver WIL can remove geographical barriers (Holmes et al., 2012; Irwin et al., 2012) and allows, for example, rural (regional) and external students to engage in WIL based activities (Peach et al., 2013).
cells.note: Systematic-review synthesis of prior work; the study reports a claimed improvement in access and participation, not a printed effect size.

O.outcome_detail: whole-blood DNA methylation at 410,746 CpGs

result.effect: 58 significant CpGs; methylation differences of 0.6% to 6.0% across the ridit scale

cells.quote: The meta-analysis identiﬁed 58 signiﬁcant CpG sites ( P < 1.2 × 10−7, Bonferroni correction for 410,746 tests) mapping to 35 genes (Fig. 1a; Supplemental Table 2). The meta-analysis effects sizes (betas) range from a difference in methyla­tion percentage of 0.6 to 6.0% between the lowest value (0) and the highest value (1) of education on the ridit scale. At 44 sites (76%), a higher education level was associated with a higher methylation level.
cells.note: Association between educational attainment and blood DNA methylation; this is not an instructional intervention.

D.treatment: higher educational attainment, adjusted for smoking status
D.comparison: lower educational attainment, adjusted for smoking status

O.outcome_detail: whole-blood DNA methylation at education-associated CpGs

result.effect: 11 CpGs genome-wide significant after smoking adjustment; average effects 28% smaller before adjustment

cells.quote: After adjusting for smoking status, the effect size for the association between educational attainment and methylation level at cg05575921 ( AHRR) was attenuated by 41% but still highly signiﬁcant (beta = 0.035, se = 0.004, p = 3.0 × 10−17; Supplemen­tal Fig. 3). In total, 11 CpGs were genome-wide signiﬁcant while adjusting for smoking status ( P < 1.2 × 10−7, Fig. 1b, Supplemental Table 2.
cells.note: The study reports adjusted associations rather than a manipulated treatment.

O.outcome_detail: whole-blood DNA methylation at the 58 education-associated CpGs

result.effect: Effects in never-smokers were on average 60% smaller; same direction at 57 of 58 sites; 27 nominally significant

cells.quote: Across all 58 CpG sites, the effect sizes in never-smokers were on average 60% smaller than in the entire dataset. Examples of CpGs for which the effect sizes in never-smokers were most similar to those in the entire population are cg23126342 in PCDH9 (beta = −0.02, se = 0.006, p = 1×1 0 −4 in never smokers), cg06695691 in SPATA5 (beta = −0.01, se = 0.004, p = 2×1 0 −4 in never smokers), and cg04907244 in SNORD93 (beta = 0.01, se = 0.004, p = 7×1 0 −4 in never smokers, respectively). These sites are characterized by small indirect effects of education in the entire population (proportion of total effect mediated by smoking = 13% for cg23126342, 8% for SPATA5 and 15% for SNORD93, respectively). For these sites, we thus see strongest evidence that methylation level correlates with educational attainment beyond effects of own smoking beha­viour; however, we note that when taking all 58 top sites, effect sizes in never-smokers were strongly correlated with effect sizes in the entire population (r = 0.83), were in the same direction at 57 sites, and were at least nominally signiﬁcant in never-smokers (p < 0.05) at 27 sites (Fig. 2b).
cells.note: Restricted observational analysis among never-smokers; no learning treatment was administered.

O.outcome_detail: suspension once or more (binary risk indicator)

cells.quote: The percentage of students who were suspended once or more was 9 percent in EWIMS schools and 9 percent in control schools; there was no statistically significant difference.
cells.note: The study reports a school-level intervention in high schools over the 2014/15 school year; it does not report learner age, prior knowledge, or a setting matching the specified categories.

O.outcome_detail: chronic absence, missing 10 percent or more of instructional time

cells.quote: The percentage of students who were chronically absent (missed 10 percent or more of instructional time) was lower in EWIMS schools (10 percent) than in control schools (14 percent); this 4 percentage point difference was statistically significant.
cells.note: The study randomly assigned 73 high schools to EWIMS or control conditions and measured outcomes after one school year.

O.outcome_detail: percentage of students with GPA of 2.0 or lower

result.effect: 17% in EWIMS schools vs 19% in control schools

cells.quote: The percentage of students who had a low GPA (2.0 or lower) was 17 percent in EWIMS schools and 19 percent in control schools; this difference was not statistically significant.
cells.note: The study reports no equivalence test or adequate-power claim, so the nonsignificant result is coded ns rather than 0.

O.outcome_detail: continuous grade point average

result.effect: Average GPA 2.98 in EWIMS schools versus 2.87 in control schools; difference 0.11 GPA points

cells.quote: However, sensitivity analyses that used continuous GPA data instead of the binary risk indicator showed that, on average, GPAs were higher in EWIMS schools (2.98) than in control schools (2.87); this difference was statistically significant.
cells.note: The study reports random assignment of schools to EWIMS or control conditions and measured GPA after the 2014/15 school year.

O.outcome_detail: percentage of students failing one or more courses

cells.quote: The percentage of students who failed one or more courses was lower in EWIMS schools (21 percent) than in control schools (26 percent); this 5 percentage point difference was statistically significant.
cells.note: The study randomly assigned 73 high schools to EWIMS or usual practices during the 2014/15 school year.

O.outcome_detail: implementation of EWIMS during the 2014/15 school year

cells.quote: "Approximately 80 percent of EWIMS schools implemented EWIMS as planned in the 2014/15 school year."
cells.note: This sentence appears in the wiki entry but not in the supplied study-text excerpt. The finding is descriptive and does not report a randomized treatment-versus-control effect.

O.outcome_detail: percentage earning insufficient credits to be on track to graduate within four years

result.effect: 14 percent in both EWIMS and control schools

cells.quote: There was not a statistically significant difference between EWIMS and control schools in the percentage of students who earned insufficient credits to be on track to graduate within four years (14 percent in both).
cells.note: The study reports a non-significant difference but does not report an equivalence test or adequate-power claim, so the direction is coded ns rather than 0.

O.outcome_detail: frequency of data review

cells.quote: In nearly all participating schools, overall implementation of the EWIMS seven-step process was low, and implementation was challenging. Nevertheless, EWIMS schools were more likely than control schools to report using an early warning system and having a dedicated team to identify and support at-risk students, but EWIMS schools did not differ from control schools in the frequency of data review or the number and type of interventions offered.
cells.note: The study reports no statistically significant difference in frequency of data review; no equivalence test or adequate-power claim is reported.
